questiontext.text:
Two parallel lines AB and CD are cut by a transversal XY. The intersections are O1 and O2. One pair of corresponding angles is shown in the diagram.

Recall: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal.


[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-1, 7, 8, -1], axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); // Points for parallel lines var A = board.create('point', [0,5], {name:'A', size:2, fixed:true}); var B = board.create('point', [7,5], {name:'B', size:2, fixed:true}); var C = board.create('point', [0,2], {name:'C', size:2, fixed:true}); var D = board.create('point', [7,2], {name:'D', size:2, fixed:true}); // Parallel lines var lineAB = board.create('line', [A, B], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2}); var lineCD = board.create('line', [C, D], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2}); // Transversal points var X = board.create('point', [1,0], {name:'X', size:2, fixed:true}); var Y = board.create('point', [4,6], {name:'Y', size:2, fixed:true}); var transversal = board.create('line', [X,Y], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:false, strokeWidth:2, dash:2}); // Intersection points var O1 = board.create('intersection', [lineAB, transversal, 0], {name:'O₁', size:2, visible:true}); var O2 = board.create('intersection', [lineCD, transversal, 0], {name:'O₂', size:2, visible:true}); // Label all four angles at O1 board.create('angle', [B, O1, Y], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'lightblue', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'red', visible:true}); board.create('angle', [Y, O1, A], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'lightgreen', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'green', visible:false}); board.create('angle', [A, O1, X], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'pink', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'red', visible:false}); board.create('angle', [X, O1, B], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'orange', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'orange', visible:false}); // Label all four angles at O2 board.create('angle', [D, O2, O1], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'lightblue', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'blue', visible:true}); board.create('angle', [O1, O2, C], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'lightgreen', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'green', visible:false}); board.create('angle', [C, O2, X], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'pink', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'red', visible:false}); board.create('angle', [X, O2, D], {radius:0.5, name: ' ', fillColor:'orange', fillOpacity:0.5, strokeColor:'orange', visible:false}); // Optional: label pairs board.create('text', [O1.X()+0.6, O1.Y()+0.4, '{#angl_corres_1#} '], {fontSize:12}); board.create('text', [O2.X()+0.5, O2.Y()+0.3, '{#angl_corres_2#} '], {fontSize:12}); board.create('text', [O1.X()-0.8, O1.Y()+0.2, ' '], {fontSize:12}); board.create('text', [O2.X()-0.8, O2.Y()+0.2, ' '], {fontSize:12}); board.create('text', [O1.X()-0.8, O1.Y()-0.3, ' '], {fontSize:12}); board.create('text', [O2.X()-0.8, O2.Y()-0.3, ' '], {fontSize:12}); board.create('text', [O1.X()+0.3, O1.Y()-0.3, ' '], {fontSize:12}); board.create('text', [O2.X()+0.3, O2.Y()-0.3, ' '], {fontSize:12}); [[/jsxgraph]]

    1. \(\angle BO_{1}Y =\) [[input:ans_angle1]] \(^{\circ}\) [[validation:ans_angle1]] [[feedback:prt_ans_angle1]]

    2. \(\angle DO_{2}O_{1} =\) [[input:ans_angle2]] \(^{\circ}\) [[validation:ans_angle2]] [[feedback:prt_ans_angle2]]

    3. \(\angle AO_{1}O_{2}=\) [[input:ans_angle3]] \(^{\circ}\) [[validation:ans_angle3]] [[feedback:prt_ans_angle3]]

    4. \(\angle CO_{2}X =\) [[input:ans_angle4]] \(^{\circ}\) [[validation:ans_angle4]] [[feedback:prt_ans_angle4]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Because they are corresponding angles, we set

\( \angle BO_1Y = \angle DO_2O_1 \quad \Rightarrow \quad {@angl_corres_1@} = {@angl_corres_2@} \)

Solving for \(x\) we get \( x = {@soln_x@} \)

Now we substitute this value of \(x\) into the angle expressions:

  • \(\angle BO_1Y = {@angl_corres_1@} = {@angl_corres_11@}^\circ\)   (Given by construction)
  • \(\angle DO_2O_1 = {@angl_corres_22@}^\circ\)   (Corresponding to \(\angle BO_1Y\))
  • \(\angle AO_1O_2 = {@angl_corres_11@}^\circ\)   (Vertical opposite to \(\angle BO_1Y\))
  • \(\angle CO_2X = {@angl_corres_22@}^\circ\)   (Vertical opposite to \(\angle DO_2O_1\))
  • \(\angle O_2O_1B = 180^\circ - {@angl_corres_11@} = {#angl_O2O1B#}^\circ\)   (Linear pair with \(\angle BO_1Y\))
  • \(\angle XO_2B = 180^\circ - \left ( {@angl_corres_22@} \right) = {#angl_XO2B#}^\circ\)   (Linear pair with \(\angle DO_2O_1\))

Solving for x we have \(\displaystyle x= {@soln_x@}\)

Therefore the size of the angles will be as follows

\(\angle BO_1Y = \displaystyle {@angl_corres_1@} \) will be \( {@angl_BO_1Y@}\)

So will,
